title: Single-motor robot arm drive
summary: One motor, several joints. Clutches pick which joint the motor moves.
points: Designed the clutches and got them working together as one transmission.
Three versions: servo-based, then solenoids I designed myself, then off-the-shelf solenoids.
Designed the PCB that drives the solenoids and wrote the firmware.
Control software is partly done.
Next up: turning it into an end effector for Universal Robots arms, instead of building a whole arm.

title: Baja SAE fuel sensor
summary: Fuel level from how the tank rattles. The tank sits on rubber mounts, so it rings over bumps, and that frequency shifts as the fuel level changes.
points: Two accelerometer boards: one right under the tank, one about 6 inches away on the frame. Subtracting them cancels the chassis, and an FFT picks out the tank's frequency.
The boards talk over CAN, so you can add as many as you want. One master board feeds the car's logging computer.
Designed the boards and firmware. The boards are being fabbed now.

title: Filament winder
summary: Keeps recycled filament a consistent width. Built to go with a Filabot EX2 extruder.
points: A magnet and a hall-effect sensor read the filament's thickness: the filament pushes the sensor away from the magnet as it passes through.
An Arduino speeds the winder up and slows it down to hold the diameter steady.
Designed the whole winder, from the frame to the motor control.
Open-sourced on Printables: 150+ downloads.

title: Backyard foundry
summary: A furnace made from an oil barrel, ceramic wool, refractory cement and a weed burner. Melts bronze (about 950 °C).
points: Cast cityscape sculptures: captured 3D geometry from Google Maps with RenderDoc, then simplified and closed the mesh in Python so it could be cast.
Made two-part molds. Also cast two bronze rings.

title: Statistical arbitrage model
summary: Nearest-neighbour forecasting on intraday price and volume: find the historical windows that most resemble a stock's recent behaviour, and read off what came next.
points: Windows of 5-minute bars are z-score normalized (price and volume as two channels) and matched by Euclidean distance against a database of historical windows ending at the same time of day. The forecast is the mean continuation of the k = 100 nearest neighbours, rescaled to the current price.
The search is partitioned across every core with multiprocessing, and ran on a 20-node cluster I built from old computers, with custom network protocols.

The auto-trader only enters when the 2-, 3- and 4-day windows all forecast the same direction past a z-score threshold. It sizes positions with the Kelly criterion, executes through the Interactive Brokers API, and exits on contrary signals or a four-hour cap.
Traded its signals live for three months (Oct 2023 to Jan 2024): 61 trades, +18.11% after fees and +39.84% before. Fees took $154 of the $288 gross.
Provisional patent filed.

title: Hygrade Precision Technologies
role: Engineering intern, then junior engineering technician · Plainville, CT
summary: Machined and inspected aerospace and defence parts to micron tolerances.
points: Parts for SpaceX Starlink, NASA Artemis, the F135 and other jet engines, and GE turbines for Navy destroyers.
Ran a CNC lathe and a manual plunge grinder, and did inspection on CMMs and with height, bore and ring gauges, calipers, micrometers and gauge blocks.
Ground the overspray off a GE destroyer-turbine bushing, back to spec, when it was holding up their line. Damaging it would have cost them about $20M in delay penalties.
Helped track down manufacturing issues across the shop's CNCs and grinders.
